title: Sutjeska and Zelengora: Maglić, Perućica and the Via Dinarica White Trail
subRegion: Sutjeska National Park, Zelengora & the upper Drina — Republika Srpska

bestPeriod.window: Mid-June–early October, with late June for the Zelengora wildflowers and September for stable rock on Maglić
bestPeriod.avoid: November–May — the Prijevor road is unploughed, katuns close and the Maglić chains ice
bestPeriod.raw: Mid-June–early October, with late June for the Zelengora wildflowers and September for stable rock on Maglić

accommodation.note: Hotel Mladost approx. 70–110 BAM pppn; katun and mountain-hut beds 30–50 BAM

food.note: Mains 12–22 BAM, a beer 3–4 BAM; katun half board 45–70 BAM

transport.note: Sarajevo transfer, hire car or driver, the rough Prijevor and Zelengora tracks

activities.note: Park entry 10 BAM pp, mandatory Perućica ranger, Trnovačko ranger fee, guide days

profile.difficultyNote: 4/5 — one 900 m ascent with chain-protected rock to the national high point, plus three plateau days at 1,500–2,000 m

gatewayAirport: SJJ Sarajevo, 2 h 45 min to Tjentište via Foča; TGD Podgorica 2 h 30 min; TIV Tivat 3 h
summary: Sutjeska is Bosnia's oldest national park and the only place in Europe where you can walk from a Yugoslav-modernist war memorial into an untouched primeval forest and up the country's highest mountain in three days. **Maglić, 2,386 m**, is a proper limestone peak with chains on its upper gully; **Perućica** is 1,400 hectares of virgin beech and fir that you may only enter with a ranger; **Zelengora** behind it is a rolling green plateau strung with a dozen glacial lakes the locals call *gorske oči*, mountain eyes. It is empty, cheap, logistically rough and among the finest walking in south-east Europe. It suits self-sufficient hikers who are comfortable with cash economies, bad roads and unmarked ground.

itinerary.title: Foča, Tjentište and the Valley of Heroes
itinerary.morning: Drive Sarajevo → Foča → **Tjentište**, roughly 2 h 45 min on the M18/M20 along the Drina and Sutjeska rivers. Pay the **10 BAM park entry in cash** at the checkpoint and register your week's plans at the National Park office.
itinerary.afternoon: Walk to the **Battle of Sutjeska memorial** — Miodrag Živković's two 19 m concrete wings from 1971, one of the great Yugoslav *spomeniks* — and the adjoining Memorial House with its Krsto Hegedušić frescoes. Then an easy 6 km along the Sutjeska river gorge.
itinerary.evening: Dinner at Hotel Mladost: *pastrmka* (Drina trout), *sač*-baked lamb, *ajvar*, and a Nektar beer. Book tomorrow's Perućica ranger at reception before the office closes.
itinerary.dayStats: 130 km drive / 2 h 45 min / Tjentište 500 m / park entry 10 BAM cash per person / 6 km riverside walk

itinerary.title: Perućica with a ranger
itinerary.morning: Meet the **National Park ranger** at 08:00 — **independent entry into Perućica is prohibited**. Drive the forest road to the **Dragoš sedlo viewpoint at about 1,500 m**, looking down the full length of one of Europe's last primeval forests, roughly 1,400 hectares of untouched beech, fir and spruce with individual trees over 300 years old and 50 m tall.
itinerary.afternoon: Descend with the ranger on the permitted line toward the **Skakavac waterfall**, a single 75 m fall at the head of the forest, then back out. Nothing here is cut, cleared or tidied: fallen trunks lie where they fell, which is the whole point of a reserve.
itinerary.evening: Back at Tjentište. Dinner at the hotel, and repack for two nights up at Prijevor with everything you need in one bag.
itinerary.dayStats: 12 km walking / 400 m ascent / Dragoš sedlo approx. 1,500 m / Skakavac approx. 75 m / ranger fee 50–100 BAM per group / 5–6 h

itinerary.title: Up to Prijevor and the Maglić summit
itinerary.morning: 4x4 or high-clearance vehicle up the rough 20 km track to **Prijevor, 1,657 m**, the saddle between Maglić and Volujak, with the katun and mountain hut and a view straight into Montenegro.
itinerary.afternoon: Climb **Maglić, 2,386 m** — Bosnia and Herzegovina's highest mountain. Grass and scree to the base of the summit wall, then the **chained gully**: roughly 80–100 m of Grade I/II rock with fixed steel chains and pegs, straightforward in the dry, genuinely serious in the wet. The summit ridge looks down on Trnovačko jezero on one side and the whole Zelengora plateau on the other.
itinerary.evening: Katun supper at Prijevor — soup, cheese pie, *pršut*, and *rakija* pressed by whoever poured it. No electricity beyond a solar lamp; the night sky here is exceptional.
itinerary.dayStats: 8 km / 730 m ascent / summit 2,386 m / chains 80–100 m at Grade I/II / 4–4 h 30 min up, 3 h down / dry from Prijevor to the top

itinerary.title: Trnovačko jezero and the Montenegrin border
itinerary.morning: From Prijevor, cross into Montenegro on foot to **Trnovačko jezero, 1,517 m** — a heart-shaped glacial lake in a cirque of grey limestone under **Trnovački Durmitor, 2,594 m**. The Montenegrin ranger collects **€1–€2 per person** in season. Be clear-eyed about this: it is an **unofficial border crossing**, tolerated in practice for day walkers but not an authorised entry point, so carry your passport, do not continue further into Montenegro, and return the same way.
itinerary.afternoon: Return over the saddle to Prijevor, then a long descent on the Via Dinarica line toward the Sutjeska valley and a transfer round to **Orlovačko jezero, 1,470 m**, on the Zelengora side.
itinerary.evening: The planinarski dom at Orlovačko has bungalows, a stove and grilled trout. Swim if you can stand 14 °C.
itinerary.dayStats: 12 km / 450 m ascent / 600 m descent / Trnovačko jezero 1,517 m / ranger €1–€2 / 5–6 h plus a 90 min transfer
itinerary.sleep: Planinarski dom / bungalows, Orlovačko jezero, 1,470 m

itinerary.title: Zelengora's mountain eyes: Donje and Gornje Bare
itinerary.morning: Walk the **Via Dinarica White Trail** west across the plateau — beech, then open pasture, then bare rolling ridges — to **Donje Bare, 1,490 m**, the most photographed of the Zelengora lakes, ringed by spruce.
itinerary.afternoon: Continue to **Gornje Bare** and over the ridge below **Bregoč (approx. 2,014 m)**, the plateau's high point, with the Maglić–Volujak–Bioč wall filling the whole southern horizon. Waymarking thins out here; keep the GPX running.
itinerary.evening: Back to Orlovačko, or on to the katun at **Kotlaničko jezero** for a night with the herds. Dinner is whatever the family cooked, in quantity.
itinerary.dayStats: 18 km / 800 m ascent / 700 m descent / Donje Bare 1,490 m / Bregoč approx. 2,014 m / 7 h realistic / marking sparse between lakes
itinerary.sleep: Katun at Kotlaničko jezero, or Orlovačko jezero

itinerary.title: Kotlaničko, Štirinsko and down to Tjentište
itinerary.morning: A loop of the eastern lakes — **Kotlaničko jezero** and **Štirinsko jezero** — on cattle traces and Via Dinarica marks, with the plateau's characteristic mix of sinkholes, springs and horse pasture.
itinerary.afternoon: Descend the old forest road and marked path off Zelengora's eastern rim to **Tjentište, 500 m**, roughly 1,000 m of loss through beech. Stay strictly on the marked line: unmarked ground in Bosnia is where the mine-risk conversation starts, and there is no reason to be off-path here.
itinerary.evening: Last dinner at Hotel Mladost or at a *vodenica* fish restaurant on the Drina near Foča — trout, *kajmak*, and Herzegovinian Blatina.
itinerary.dayStats: 19 km / 400 m ascent / 1,000 m descent / Tjentište 500 m / 7 h realistic / stay on marked trail

itinerary.title: The Drina, Foča and out
itinerary.morning: Drive north down the Drina. If you have half a day, the **Tara river canyon** and the rafting put-in above Foča are 40 minutes away, and the Drina's confluence with the Ćehotina at Foča is a good stop for the Aladža mosque, rebuilt in 2019.
itinerary.afternoon: Continue to Sarajevo (2 h 45 min) for Baščaršija, the Latin Bridge and the Tunnel of Hope, or south-west to Mostar (3 h) if you are flying from Dubrovnik.
itinerary.evening: *Ćevapi* at Željo or Petica in Sarajevo, Bosnian coffee in a copper *džezva*, and the flight out the following morning.
itinerary.dayStats: Tjentište–Sarajevo 130 km / 2 h 45 min / Tjentište–Mostar approx. 3 h / spend leftover BAM before the border, it is not convertible abroad

accommodationStrategy.name: Hotel Mladost
accommodationStrategy.description: The only real hotel inside the park, a socialist-era block that has been progressively renovated, with the memorial 300 m away, the park office at reception, secure parking and a restaurant. Roughly 70–110 BAM per person. It is where you arrange the Perućica ranger and the Prijevor 4x4, which is worth more than the room.

accommodationStrategy.name: Prijevor katun
accommodationStrategy.description: A working shepherd station and simple hut on the saddle beneath Maglić, reachable only by rough track. Blankets, a wood stove, an outside tap and no electricity — and the only bed that makes a Maglić ascent a half-day rather than an epic. 30–50 BAM, cash, booked by phone the day before.

accommodationStrategy.name: Planinarski dom Orlovačko jezero
accommodationStrategy.description: Wooden bungalows and a hikers' house beside a lake on the Zelengora side, with a kitchen, trout, and vehicle access for luggage. It is the natural base for two plateau days and much warmer at night than a katun. 40–70 BAM per person.

logistics.connectivity: **Bosnia and Herzegovina is outside the EU roaming zone.** The Western Balkans regional roaming agreement covers movement between the six regional economies, not EU visitors; EU SIMs are charged at reduced but non-zero non-EU rates. Buy an m:tel or BH Telecom prepaid SIM in Sarajevo or Foča. There is **no signal at Prijevor, on most of Zelengora, or in Perućica**. Download offline maps and the Via Dinarica GPX before you leave Foča.
logistics.emergency: 112 general, 122 police, 124 ambulance. Mountain rescue is the volunteer GSS; **there is no routine helicopter service** and a ground evacuation from Zelengora will take most of a day. Nearest hospitals: Foča (which has a university clinical centre) and Sarajevo. **EHIC/GHIC is not valid in Bosnia** — insure for mountain walking to 2,500 m plus repatriation, and note that a rescue at Trnovačko jezero involves Montenegro.
logistics.weather: Afternoon thunderstorms build over Maglić and Volujak from around 14:00 in July and August, and the summit chains are a poor place for one — start by 08:00. Zelengora holds fog well into the morning after a cold night. Snow is possible above 1,800 m in any month.
logistics.bookingWindows: Perućica rangers 1–2 days ahead through the Tjentište office, more on August weekends. Prijevor katun and the 4x4 transfer 2–3 days. Hotel Mladost 2–4 weeks in summer. Nothing here uses an online booking portal; phone and Viber are the channels.
logistics.money: The currency is the **convertible mark (BAM/KM), pegged at 1 EUR = 1.95583 BAM**. Euros are sometimes accepted at poor rates; **use marks**. **There is no ATM inside the national park** — draw 400–600 BAM in Foča or Sarajevo before you go up, in small notes. Cards work at Hotel Mladost and nowhere above it. Tipping is rounding up, or 10% for a full meal.
logistics.transportRules: No vignette in Bosnia; roads are tolled only on the A1. **Cross-border rental permissions matter here** — confirm your hire contract allows Montenegro and Croatia, and that the green card lists them, before driving anywhere near Trnovačko. The Prijevor track needs genuine ground clearance; hiring a local driver is cheaper than the damage waiver. The Tjentište–Sarajevo M20 is scenic and slow.
logistics.permits: Park entry 10 BAM per person, cash. **Perućica may only be entered with a National Park ranger — independent access is prohibited and enforced.** Camping is restricted to designated areas at Tjentište; wild camping in Perućica and the strict reserve is forbidden. Fires outside katun hearths are prohibited. Drones need park permission. Do not remove deadwood or plants from Perućica.
logistics.health: **Landmine awareness is a real and non-negotiable part of walking in Bosnia.** The national park's core routes are cleared and in regular use, but BiH still has suspected hazardous areas and the rule is absolute: **stay on marked, worn trails, never shortcut through untrodden ground, never enter ruins, trenches or fenced areas, and heed any red-and-white skull-and-crossbones or "MINE" sign.** Check BHMAC guidance before travelling. Elsewhere: treat all water, expect livestock guardian dogs at katuns (stop, do not run), and note that ticks and TBE are present in the beech forest up to about 1,500 m.

proTips: Arrange the **Perućica ranger and the Prijevor 4x4 on your first evening**, in person at the Tjentište office or hotel reception. Phone and email in advance frequently go unanswered; showing up and booking face to face works.
Draw **BAM cash in Foča**, not Tjentište. There is no ATM in the park, katuns cannot change a €50, and euros above the valley get you a bad rate at best.

Climb Maglić on your **second day at Prijevor** if the forecast allows a choice — the chains dry within a couple of hours of sun, and wet limestone in that gully is what turns a Grade I scramble into an accident.
Ask the Prijevor katun to point out the Trnovačko path before you set off. The border saddle is obvious in clear weather and not obvious at all in cloud.

Treat **Trnovačko jezero as an out-and-back day walk**, not a route into Montenegro. Continuing to Gusinje or Plav from there without an official crossing is an immigration problem you do not want in the Balkans.

Carry a GPX for Zelengora specifically. The Via Dinarica marks are good in principle and intermittent in practice between Donje Bare and Kotlaničko, where the ground is open pasture with cattle traces in every direction.
Buy cheese and *kajmak* at the katuns. It is the entire local economy up there, it costs a few marks, and it is better than anything in Sarajevo.

Go in the **last week of June** for the Zelengora meadows or the **first fortnight of September** for Maglić. July and August bring heat on the Sutjeska valley floor and the only crowds the park ever sees.
Spend your leftover marks before you cross out. BAM is a closed currency and is effectively worthless once you leave.

raw.Hut-to-hut booking path: There is no formal hut chain here. The sequence is **Hotel Mladost at Tjentište (500 m, park-owned)** → **the katun and mountain hut at Prijevor (1,657 m)** → **the planinarski dom and bungalows at Orlovačko jezero (1,470 m)** → **the katun at Kotlaničko jezero / Zelengora** → back to Tjentište. All bookings go **direct by phone or Viber/WhatsApp to the operator, or through the National Park Sutjeska office at Tjentište**; nothing is on a booking portal, and email replies are slow. **Everything is cash in convertible marks (BAM)** — expect **30–50 BAM (€15–€26) for a bed** and **45–70 BAM (€23–€36) for half board** at a katun, and **70–110 BAM per person** at Hotel Mladost. **There are no card terminals above Tjentište and no ATM inside the park.** Bring a **sleeping-bag liner and a light sleeping bag** — katun bedding is blankets, and the huts sit at 1,500–1,700 m where August nights fall to 4–6 °C. **If a katun is full**, the shepherd family will make space on the floor or in a second building; there is no alternative within walking distance, so ring ahead the day before rather than turning up.
raw.Ranger permits and park fees: Park entry is **10 BAM / €5 per person**, collected at the checkpoint on the M20 at Tjentište, **cash only**. **Entry to Perućica is strictly guided and independent access is prohibited** — you must be accompanied by a National Park ranger, arranged the day before at the Tjentište office, with a guide fee typically **50–100 BAM per group** depending on size and route. The standard visit is the **Dragoš sedlo viewpoint** over the forest and the **Skakavac waterfall (about 75 m)**; walking into the forest floor itself is permitted only on the ranger's chosen line. **A separate ranger sits seasonally at Trnovačko jezero on the Montenegrin side and collects €1–€2 per person.**
raw.Safety markers and waymarking: Bosnia uses the standard ex-Yugoslav **planinarska markacija — a red circle with a white centre** (the same family as Slovenia's Knafelc blaze), painted on rock and tree, plus wooden signposts giving hours. The **Via Dinarica White Trail**, the alpine line of the three-corridor Via Dinarica network, is additionally marked with its own **blue-and-white logo** and crosses Zelengora and Sutjeska. Marking quality is good on the Maglić and Perućica routes and around Orlovačko, and **poor to absent on the Zelengora plateau between lakes**, where the "path" is often a cattle trace. Carry a GPX. **There are no via ferratas**, but Maglić's upper gully has **fixed chains and steel pegs over roughly 80–100 m of Grade I/II rock**.
raw.Elevation and gear essentials: High points: **Maglić 2,386 m** (the highest mountain in Bosnia and Herzegovina), Trnovački Durmitor 2,594 m on the Montenegrin side, Bregoč on Zelengora at about 2,014 m, Prijevor 1,657 m, Trnovačko jezero 1,517 m. Cumulative ascent across the walking days is roughly **3,200 m**. **Snow lies in the Maglić north gully and the Zelengora shaded corries into late June**; before 25 June carry microspikes. Gloves for the chains, a helmet if there is any party above you in the gully, and B-rated boots. No ferrata set needed, though a short sling and carabiner is reassuring on the chains in the wet.
raw.Water, food resupply and rubbish: Zelengora is unusually well watered for karst — springs, streams and lakes throughout — but the plateau is grazed by cattle and horses all summer, so **filter or treat everything**. The Maglić route from Prijevor is **dry from the katun to the summit**: carry 2 litres. Katuns sell milk, *kajmak*, cheese, *pita* and coffee for a few marks. **Resupply only in Foča or Tjentište**; there is no shop in the park interior. **All rubbish comes out with you** — the park has minimal collection and burning is the local default.
raw.Bail-out options, rescue and insurance: Prijevor is reachable by 4x4 on a rough 20 km track from Tjentište, so a Maglić evacuation is a drive, not a carry. Orlovačko has vehicle access. The remote stretch is the Zelengora plateau between Kotlaničko and Donje Bare, which is 3–4 hours from a road. **112 is the general emergency number; 122 police and 124 ambulance also work.** Mountain rescue is the volunteer **GSS (Gorska služba spašavanja)** and there is **no routine helicopter rescue** — plan on a ground evacuation taking most of a day. **Bosnia is outside the EU and EHIC/GHIC does not apply**; buy insurance naming Bosnia and Herzegovina, mountain walking to 2,500 m, and repatriation. Note that a rescue at Trnovačko jezero may involve **Montenegrin** services, which is a separate jurisdiction and a separate insurance question.
raw.Realistic walking times: Bosnian signposts and shepherd estimates are quick. Add **30–35%**. Prijevor to Maglić is quoted at 3 h; plan 4–4 h 30 min with the chains and any queue. Prijevor to Trnovačko jezero is quoted 1 h 30 min–2 h; plan 2 h–2 h 30 min.

sources.verified: Sutjeska National Park entry at **10 BAM / €5 per person, cash only** at the checkpoint; that **entry into Perućica is strictly guided and independent access is prohibited by park regulation**; **Trnovačko jezero at 1,517 m** on the Bosnia–Montenegro border, reached in **1.5–2 hours from the Prijevor saddle**, with a **seasonal Montenegrin ranger collecting €1–€2 per person**; Maglić at 2,386 m as the country's highest mountain; the BAM peg to the euro.
sources.confidenceNotes: The Perućica ranger fee is quoted as a range and is negotiated per group — confirm with the Tjentište office. Katun and mountain-hut rates at Prijevor, Orlovačko and Kotlaničko are 2025 estimates set in cash and vary by family; none is bookable online. The precise length and grade of the fixed chains on Maglić, and Bregoč's elevation on Zelengora, should be spot-checked against a current Bosnian hiking club description. Hotel Mladost's operating status and renovation state have changed repeatedly — re-verify before publishing. The legal status of the on-foot crossing to Trnovačko jezero is grey and locally tolerated rather than formally authorised; this should be checked with the park and worded carefully. Landmine guidance must be re-verified against the current BHMAC map before publication. Perućica's protected area is variously cited between about 1,400 and 1,500 hectares, and the Skakavac waterfall between 70 and 80 m.
